title: withdrawRewardToken does not gate on dispatcherHook.mintDebt — pending mint debt can be stranded by a premature sweep
description: `withdrawRewardToken` requires `totalStaked == 0 && paused()` but does not require `dispatcherHook.mintDebt() == 0` or call `_syncBudget()` to pull pending mint debt before sweeping. If owner/migrator triggers the sweep while a non-zero `mintDebt` is still owed by the BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook (e.g. between an interaction that registered debt and the next `pull()`), the sweep takes only the current on-chain balance to `to`. After the sweep, when `pull()` is eventually called (by anyone via stake/unstake on a re-staked pool, or by `pullAndRefresh` if the contract resumes), the freshly-minted phUSD lands in the (now empty, paused, post-sunset) staker. It is not lost — `withdrawRewardToken` can be called again — but the assumption documented in the plan ('sweep the full runway') is partially broken: a single call sweeps less than the full `V = balance + mintDebt`. The protocol must remember to call `pullAndRefresh` (or just `_syncBudget`-equivalent) first.
impact: Operational risk, not direct economic loss. The sweep operator must remember to drain mintDebt before the sweep, or the sweep will under-deliver. Worst case: a small residual phUSD pools in the staker after sunset until a follow-up sweep. Note: `pullAndRefresh` is `onlyOwner`, so the migrator alone (without owner) cannot drain mintDebt — they can only sweep on-chain balance. If the trust model assumes the migrator can fully decommission the contract, this is a gap.
recommendation: Add `_syncBudget()` (or just the dispatcherHook.pull() leg) inline at the top of `withdrawRewardToken` so the sweep always operates against the full `V`. This is cheap (a single external call) and removes the operational footgun. Alternative: add a check `require(address(dispatcherHook) == address(0) || dispatcherHook.mintDebt() == 0, 'NFTStakerV2: pending mint debt')` so the sweep cannot run with stranded debt, forcing the operator to pull first.
attack_scenario:
Operator error scenario:
1. NFTStakerV2 is funded and running per plan.
2. Migration completes; totalStaked is driven to zero either organically or via unstakeFor.
3. Between the last interaction and the sweep, the BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook has accumulated mintDebt > 0 (e.g. from continued V3 pooler activity — the hook is shared infrastructure).
4. Owner pauses, calls `withdrawRewardToken(to, balance)`. Sweeps only the on-chain balance. The pending mintDebt is not realised.
5. Operator now believes the staker is fully drained, but a subsequent `pull()` (from any hook caller) would deposit fresh phUSD into the (paused, empty) contract.
6. Operator must remember a second sweep cycle.

This is not exploitable by a malicious party — only the owner/migrator can drain — but it is an intent-vs-implementation gap given the plan's framing of withdrawRewardToken as 'the decommissioning sweep that would have prevented the ~910 phUSD orphaning in the current incident' (plan line 205-206). A single-call sweep that misses mintDebt does not prevent orphaning.
